analysis.investment_thesis: Aavas Financiers is a rare-quality affordable HFC with a 29.7% net profit CAGR over 7 years, a differentiated rural/semi-urban focus that keeps competition low, and a forward P/E of just 13.56x — one of the most attractively priced growth stories in the financial services space today.
key_strengths: Exceptional compounding track record: net profit grew from INR 93 Cr (FY18) to INR 574 Cr (FY25) at 29.7% CAGR — consistent, uninterrupted growth across 7 years including COVID
Rural and semi-urban low-income focus creates a natural moat — most large HFCs and banks do not serve this customer economically, limiting competitive intensity
Forward P/E of 13.56x is deeply attractive for a business growing earnings at 25%+ — PEG well below 1.0
key_risks: Promoter holding at 48.95% (marginally below 50%) is a yellow flag in the Indian context — any further dilution below 45% would be concerning
ROE of 13.9% is below best-in-class HFCs at similar growth rates — needs improvement as book matures and leverage optimizes
D/E at 3.08x is the highest among comparable peers — any liquidity squeeze in wholesale funding could stress ALM
red_flags: Promoter below 50% is unusual for a high-conviction Indian financial services bet — needs monitoring for further dilution
Finance cost data for FY25 (INR 5 Cr vs INR 828 Cr in FY24) appears to be a data anomaly — underlying borrowing costs remain elevated
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Aavas Financiers, based in Jaipur and focused on Rajasthan, MP, and Gujarat semi-urban markets, has built one of the cleanest affordable HFC franchises in India. Revenue has grown from INR 494 Cr (FY18) to INR 1,988 Cr (FY25) — a 22% CAGR — while net profit scaled from INR 93 Cr to INR 574 Cr. The business has not missed a beat across COVID, interest rate cycles, and liquidity crises. Balance sheet assets have grown from INR 7,657 Cr to INR 18,618 Cr, funded largely by borrowings (D/E 3.08x) but offset by strong equity growth (INR 2,098 Cr → INR 4,361 Cr).

The forward P/E of 13.56x is the standout valuation opportunity — if earnings grow at even 20% next year, you're buying a quality compounder at less than 1x PEG. The risk here is the promoter holding (48.95%) and somewhat lower ROE (13.9%) vs AADHARHFC (16.9%). But Aavas's niche positioning in truly underserved rural credit markets gives it a longer growth runway with less competition. This is a BUY for a 5-year horizon.
